applies_why: The judge gives an UNDERDETERMINED verdict for Acts 2:30, so K-S2 governs whether that verdict rests on single-verse nonstatement or on treating a two-sense verse as open.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED': I weighed whether this forbids any UNDERDETERMINED verdict when a single verse lacks the link versus forbidding only citing that single-verse nonstatement as the ground; the judge's text reads as the latter.
why: The judge rests UNDERDETERMINED on the two chains not forcing each other after both sides' multi-verse support, not on the fact that a single verse fails to state the link or its contrary, and it does not treat a two-sense verse as open.
